claims.explanation: Triptolide covalently inhibits XPB/ERCC3, a TFIIH subunit required for RNA polymerase II transcription and nucleotide excision repair, causing rapid RNAPII degradation and apoptosis. Selectivity likely reflects dependence on high transcriptional output and intact apoptotic execution, so lines with wild-type TP53 and high ERCC3/RELA expression are most sensitive, while TP53-mutant or low-transcription lines are protected.

features.basis: TP53-mutant lines are enriched among least affected; loss of p53-mediated apoptosis reduces triptolide killing
XPB/ERCC3 is the direct triptolide target; higher target expression increases drug engagement
NF-kB/RELA is an annotated triptolide target and mediates inflammatory/apoptotic signaling
BRAF-mutant melanoma and thyroid lines are enriched among sensitive lines, suggesting MAPK-driven transcriptional dependence
KRAS-mutant pancreatic and lung lines are enriched among resistant lines, suggesting oncogene-associated resistance
SMARCA4-mutant lines appear in the resistant set, possibly through chromatin remodeling that reduces transcriptional dependence
CDKN2A loss is common in resistant lines and may reflect altered cell-cycle/apoptotic thresholds
ARID1A-mutant lines are enriched among resistant lines, suggesting SWI/SNF loss reduces sensitivity
NFE2L2-mutant esophageal and bladder lines appear in the sensitive set, possibly through oxidative-stress vulnerability
EGFR-mutant esophageal lines are among sensitive lines, suggesting EGFR-driven transcriptional addiction
ATM-mutant thyroid line is sensitive, consistent with impaired DNA repair enhancing triptolide-induced damage
IAP family anti-apoptotic proteins can confer resistance to apoptosis-inducing therapies
